title: SLO threshold jump investigation and automated shedding playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-02-09 at ~03:40 UTC we observed a sudden SLO budget burn for text-generation p99 latency for customers pinned to region-us-west-2. Automated region failover and traffic routing moved a large percentage of traffic to region-eu-west-1 which caused downstream circuit breakers in the eu cluster to open and aggressive load-shedding to trigger. The net result was a 42% SLO miss window for the affected routes and visible client errors for high-throughput customers.

Root cause (high level): A recent kernel scheduling change (batch-optimizer v2) increased median KV cache miss penalty for cold prefixes on longer sequences. This raised tail latency in us-west-2 for a subset of models. Smart-routing detected latency SLO violations and shifted requests to eu-west-1, but eu-west-1's circuit-breaker hysteresis and threshold parameters were tuned for a different traffic shape. Combined with cold cache and shorter autoscaling cooldown, the eu cluster tripped breakers quickly, shed load, and then flapped while autoscaling attempted to recover.

Key metrics during incident: error-budget consumed: 1.5 hours equivalent over 55 minutes; p50/p95/p99 latency delta (pre->incident) on route /v1/generate: 18ms -> 32ms -> 140ms; amplified rerouted traffic: +62% to eu-west-1 within 4m; circuit-breaker open events: 87 in 12m.

Timeline (condensed):
- 03:38 UTC: batch-optimizer v2 rollout to us-west-2 completed for runtime-1.20.
- 03:40 UTC: gradual increase in p99 observed; automated smart-routing picks up SLO drift at 03:42.
- 03:46 UTC: traffic redirected to eu-west-1 via fallback policy.
- 03:50 UTC: eu-west-1 CPU queues and KV cache miss rates spike; circuit breakers open at 03:51.
- 03:58 UTC: shedding rules kick in; client 429s observed.
- 04:35 UTC: remediation actions (partial rollback and temporary expand of autoscaling max) complete; SLOs start to recover by 04:50.

Contributing factors (detailed):
- Kernel scheduling change increased slow-path for cold KV cache.
- Smart-routing policy had a low-cost bias that prioritized latency signals without considering capacity hysteresis in target regions.
- Circuit breaker hysteresis windows were asymmetric across regions and tuned for steady-state, not surge of redirected traffic.
- Autoscaler cooldown and target CPU thresholds caused premature scale-down in eu-west-1 before the influx.
- Lack of cross-region pre-warm cache strategy for mirrored prefixes allowed cold starts to amplify latency.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back batch-optimizer v2 to runtime-1.19 in us-west-2 at 04:10 UTC (partial rollback for 60% of traffic).
- Increased eu-west-1 autoscaling max for the cluster and extended cooldown to 6 minutes.
- Temporarily raised circuit-breaker error threshold by +40% to avoid flapping for 25 minutes.

Links to artifacts:
- Incident report (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/33021/regional-shed-incident
- Grafana dashboard (latency and CB events): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/multi-region-slo
- GitHub PR for rollback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Runtime kernel change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4798

Postmortem hypothesis and validation plan:
- Hypothesis: the batch-optimizer v2 changed batching/kernels in a way that increased cold-path decode latency; when traffic was redirected this exposure tripled the effective p99. Validate by replaying production traces on runtime-1.20 with warm and cold cache states and comparing tail latency.
- Validation plan: synthetic load replay, cache-warmup experiment, and A/B rollout against small traffic fraction for 48 hours with elevated tracing.

Desired state / success criteria:
- Smart-routing becomes sensitive to target-region capacity hysteresis signals (not just latency) and avoids redirect storms.
- Circuit-breaker configuration synchronized across regions with explicit surge profiles.
- KV cache pre-warm strategy reduces cold-path tail for mirrored prefixes and recently promoted model variants.
